protocol.question: does a selected long/flat rule hold up in later complete intraday windows, costs, slower orders and related markets?

window.calendar: fixed Monday-Friday UTC candidates, not a verified exchange calendar

momentum.rule: latest completed close minus first open of the last n completed five-minute bars, positive means long; price points, not percentage or n-lag close

mean_reversion.rule: latest close minus mean of last n completed closes INCLUDING latest, divided by sample std ddof=1; enter z<=-entry_z, exit z>=0; insufficient or zero variance flat

protocol.feature_policy: only exact complete five-minute buckets; reset prices, latent holding state, pending orders and position per UTC date; no warmup orders or latent holding; twelve bars fit the sixty-minute warmup

selection.metric: development net daily account-capital Sharpe in base
selection.tie_break: fewer filled entries, then lexical configuration id
selection.later_use: keep NQ development choice in later NQ and ES/YM; no replacement if ineligible

execution.position: one full contract long or flat; capital convention, no margin simulation or equal-risk sizing
execution.fill: observed minute open proxy at or after completed-bar end plus extra delay, not a quote at that instant; directional tick rounding then adverse ticks
execution.terminal: known before the window; cancel all pending signal orders at 11:50; exit first observed open at/after 11:50+delay and strictly before 12:00; missing exit fails unresolved
execution.entry: decisions at/after 09:00, entries fill strictly before 11:30; an unfilled signal is superseded by a later decision
execution.baseline: intraday_long first eligible 09:00 instruction plus delay; same cutoff, costs, mask and terminal instruction

statistics.uncertainty: paired circular blocks of ordered eligible windows; conventional 252 scaling, descriptive; calendar gaps and longer memory remain limits

protocol.eligibility: ex-post exact 240-minute windows only; same source-quality mask for all rules, baselines and scenarios; retrospective conditional returns, not a live 09:00 filter
protocol.cross_market: own complete-window results and separately paired intersection of NQ/ES/YM complete UTC dates; keep the NQ own-window development pick
protocol.prior_exposure: wholly synthetic seeded software fixture; no market inference
protocol.source_boundary: opaque source_segment_id per source rule and UTC date, contract identity unknown; calendar continuity inferred from historical date semantics plus exact local cache provenance, not recovered instrument IDs
protocol.revision_rule: coverage can justify a documented new lock before strategy results; performance cannot change the protocol quietly

readiness.basis: historical source-rule inference within UTC date only
